Perfect! The fix works. The key change was to sort all items by count (descending, using the negative) and then alphabetically (ascending), then take the top n. This ensures that:
1. Items are primarily ordered by frequency (highest first)
2. When frequencies are tied, they're sorted alphabetically
3. We get the correct n items considering the full sorted order
